final.title: Health values typed in chat: the transcript, the recall index, embeddings, compaction and claims
final.question: When a conversation row carries a health value (typed by the owner, or said back by Waldo in an owner-channel reply), which stores may keep the value, which get only a value-free form, who decides that a row carries one, and where does that answer live?
final.today:
Observed at beta-mvp e5c022ef unless marked.

1. The transcript keeps every row verbatim. The canonical store scrubs only secret URLs (packages/runtime/src/conversation/canonical-owner-store.ts:19-22, applied in save at :150; persistOwnerInput at :193). The Telegram store does the same (channels/conversation-store.ts:54-56). Telegram turns use the legacy conv:* store (channels/owner-do.ts:2554, :2750). App turns use the canonical store wrapped by the index (:2814). iMessage turns use the canonical store without the index wrapper (:2820).

2. The episode index keeps rows verbatim. It is an FTS5 table in the owner object (channels/episodes.ts:51). The owner's message is indexed when it is stored, before the turn runs (:141-145). Saved rows follow (:146-152). The boot backfill indexes appPayload as is, and only when the index is empty (:157-163). Compaction rows are skipped (:128-130). Readers:
- search_episodes, a tool the model calls (search maps the stored speaker to owner at :72);
- B3 per-turn recall (memory/turn-recall.ts:42-55, line format at :62), limited to rows the chain may reach (channels/app-threads.ts:37-42);
- the nightly pass (owner-do.ts:3031-3039), which reads index text into a model call and writes claims. It looks back at most 7 days (episodes.ts:189).
All three readers put text into model context. The nightly pass's only persistent output is claims.

3. Claims can hold a numeric value the owner stated, and it reaches every turn's system prompt. remember stores an owner-grounded claim and its verbatim quote (tools/live/memory.ts:50-71). Health is a profile kind (memory/claims.ts:19-21). The per-turn prompt is turnMemoryPrompt (claims.ts:1056-1075), called at channels/owner-turn.ts:546. The pinned tests assert the value is in that prompt (test/memory-health-contact-route.test.ts:28; test/memory-health-owner-turn.test.ts:37-38). The pre-tool destination for remember is internal_context (hooks/registry.ts:904-917), where the free-text health scan is off for null-taint text (scribe/sanitiser.ts:585-590). NIGHTLY_MEMORY_INSTRUCTION (claims.ts:1111) does not ask the model to leave numbers out. memory_backups holds claim payloads (claims.ts:633-637). read_memory has an optional resolveSource dependency (tools/live/memory.ts:20). Only forget_memory reads it (:101), and production wiring passes none (owner-do.ts:2759-2780).

4. What rejects health today:
- the generic floor at memory_block, r2_summary and the other destinations (packages/contracts/src/memory/sanitise.ts:349-362);
- the numeric check on a compaction summary (owner-turn.ts:745-746), using numericHealthIn (scribe/sanitiser.ts:90-91).
numericHealthIn is built from English keyword regexes for sensor and score shapes (sanitiser.ts:69-91). A verifier's scratch run found it misses lab-value and dose sentences, including the pinned fixture's text. [inference] I confirmed the patterns by reading them; the fixture has no keyword they match.

5. Compaction is built and switched off (conversation/compaction.ts:7-8). Its input is the model view of the chain (compaction.ts:82-85, conversationModelMessages). Every turn already sends that view to the same provider with store:false (llm/openai.ts:70). Its instruction asks for qualitative health only (:24). The approved draft keeps policy (a) and the numeric floor (docs/proposals/ADR_DRAFT_CONVERSATION_COMPACTION_ROW_2026-10-13.md:38-39, :69). The floor is in code (owner-turn.ts:741-746). compactIfDue has no caller in owner-do.ts yet (defined at owner-turn.ts:723, exposed at :759); the B2 post-delivery call has not landed.

6. Semantic recall (B4) is specified, not built. The spec promises "health never embedded" and picks bge-m3 for mixed English, Hindi and Marathi (#1103 comment 6154593035, as recorded in claude/backend-lead-log c43c415c, LOG.md:232). No field anywhere says which row is health. A regex would be a fixed rule making a judgment call (CLAUDE.md:11).

7. App UX: the transcript page sends each row's appPayload verbatim (channels/app-api.ts:197-218, text at :211). The owner must see their own words on every device. Thread titles already use the value-free pattern (channels/app-threads.ts:53-58).

8. Forget is literal. It redacts conversation rows, witnesses and episode rows by needle (conversation-store.ts:165-200; owner-do.ts:2761-2778; claims.ts:626-632). Thread erase deletes the chain prefix and index rows (owner-do.ts:990-997). Account deletion calls storage.deleteAll() (owner-do.ts:919, :1483, :1611), so any new owner-object table is covered.

9. Health consent withdrawal is a Supabase RPC sent from the edge route (channels/app-health.ts:145, :157). No owner-object path observes it; owner-do.ts has no withdrawal handling.

10. Open PR #1248 (claude/bounded-history-load) makes load() read only the window, not the whole chain.

11. Conflicting text:
- The retained contract asks for deterministic DLP classification and a quarantine before any transcript write (docs/planning/waldo-agent-mvp/IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACTS.md:15-17, :39). It also requires deletion and revocation generations that late writers check (:37, :41). It says newer explicit decisions control (:3).
- docs/app/CONSULT_VERDICTS.md:39 lists owner-typed health numbers in transcripts as an open owner ruling. Ruling 2 (HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:7) answered it for model context; it is still open for transcripts and the stores built from them.
constraints: CLAUDE.md:11: judgment belongs to the model. Whether a row carries a health value is a judgment, so no regex classifies. Deterministic rejection only at hard boundaries; medication dosing is one. The ADR-0024 numeric floor at a persistent write qualifies as a backstop, never as the classifier.
Brain ADR-0081 line 80: 'Never' means the schema and the sanitiser reject the field. A rule enforced only by a model class must not be published as 'never'.

Brain ADR-0081 line 90: a user-stated numeric goal persists in the per-user DO as quoted user intent until the user edits or deletes it. This is the closest precedent for owner-stated numbers kept in DO storage.

Brain ADR-0081 retention (lines 84-87) and withdrawal (lines 111, 113): withdrawal deletes reconstructive residues, including DO run residues. HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:27 sets raw retention at 90 days and says withdrawing model use alone stops Waldo using health in conversation.
HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:7 (ruling 2): the owner's readings and derived context may reach model context and owner-channel replies end to end.
HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:23: long-term memory holds qualitative patterns plus a pointer; numeric evidence stays in the Supabase health plane.
HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:9: withdrawal-purge scope is a hard gate before any outside user.

CLAUDE.md:23: never logs, audit records, R2 summaries, browser jobs, third-party sends or drafts (unless the owner asks to share an item), externally tainted paths, or bulk long-term memory. Sensitive chat is classified at ingress.
CLAUDE.md:17: conversation-body storage and new health-pattern persistence need explicit bounded ADR review.
CLAUDE.md:18: intent before I/O, one retry owner, bounded work, cancellation fencing, honest terminal ambiguity. No model or embedding call inside the owning SQLite transaction.
IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACTS.md:37, :41 and build plan :275: deletion and revocation advance a generation that late writers check; derived stores respect source and consent generations.
CLAUDE.md:22: memory is correctable context, not permission. A class must never widen a destination or authorise cross-surface replay.
The owner sees their own messages verbatim (app-api.ts:211). No app.v1 break without a contract-first change.
Provider egress uses store:false (HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:24). Staging traces may capture text for opted-in testers in alpha and beta only; production never.

Brain's ADR folder is append-only (waldo-brain CLAUDE.md, protected files). security-checklist.md is a mirrored rule whose canonical copy lives in Brain (MIRROR-SYNC.md). A backend ADR cannot edit either.
channels/owner-do.ts has a single writer (the Mac lane). channels/episodes.ts is also changed by the B4 lane. #1248 changes canonical-owner-store.ts load().
Hosted migrations, wrangler.jsonc, new third-party services, deploys and Brain merges are the owner's actions.

options.name: Quarantine at ingress
options.what: The retained contract, with model classification in place of DLP. A model call classifies each inbound row before it persists. Values go to a new owner-only Supabase table. The transcript holds a marker and an opaque ref that every reader resolves.
options.pros:
- Values live in one RLS plane with the health plane's retention and withdrawal purge.
- Strongest Art-9 posture. Matches IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACTS.md:17, :39.
- Every store built from the transcript sees only markers.
options.cons:
- Size L across two repositories.
- The classify call must finish before the row persists, or a crash loses the input. Today the store persists first (canonical-owner-store.ts:193).
- A hosted migration (owner action), an ADR-0081 amendment, and an app.v1 change.
- Every reader resolves refs: app, Telegram and iMessage history, compaction, forget, export. A new device shows markers until resolution works.
- [inference] The value already crossed Telegram or Apple and the model provider, so this protects only Waldo's copy.
- Risk: high.

options.name: Verbatim everywhere (amend ADR-0081)
options.what: A health value in a conversation row may persist verbatim in every store: transcript, index, embeddings, compaction summaries and claims. Forget reaches each one, Vectorize included.
options.pros:
- Least work (S).
- Best recall, including semantic recall over health questions.
options.cons:
- Contradicts HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:23 and the approved compaction policy (a).
- Reverses B4's 'health never embedded'. Vec2Text recovered 92% of 32-token inputs exactly on the models tested (Morris et al., EMNLP 2023). [inference] bge-m3 was not tested; similar risk.
- Vectorize mutations are asynchronous, so forget needs a read-back.
- Exact values keep riding every turn's system prompt through claims.
- Risk: high privacy, low engineering.

options.name: Light split: verbatim transcript and index, model class gates new stores and claims
options.what:
- The transcript and its FTS episode index keep rows verbatim. Both sit in the owner object, under the same forget, thread-erase and deleteAll reach. Every index reader feeds model context, which ruling 2 allows.
- Compaction flips on its approved policy (a) and numeric floor. No new gate.
- The model writes one class per row at ingress (none, qualitative, values) into a new owner-object table, row_class, with a value-free restatement for values rows. Only new stores read it: B4 embeds class none only, plus a numeric-floor hard gate. A missing or failed class means not embedded.
- Claims hold a qualitative statement plus a source_ref pointer. The model decides by instruction; the numeric floor is the backstop. read_memory resolves the exact value from the source row as model context, within the chain's recall reach.
- Before outside users: withdrawal and retention rewrite values rows to their value-free form, using the class.
options.pros:
- The owner sees their words verbatim everywhere. No app.v1, Supabase, wrangler or edge change.
- Compaction is unblocked now, by the ruling alone.
- No index rewrite, no backlog that stalls search, nightly or compaction. A failed class fails closed and blocks nothing.
- 'Health never embedded' and 'qualitative plus pointer' become enforceable, decided by the model.
- Values leave the every-turn system prompt.
- One class answer serves embeddings, withdrawal, retention and later A3 visibility (narrowing only).
- Size M overall before outside users; the withdrawal slice is L.
options.cons:
- The index keeps values for as long as the transcript does. This is right only if the owner reads the index as part of the transcript record, not as long-term memory under amendment:23.
- One cheap model call per owner turn. [inference] Small; the build PR measures it.
- Misclassified values rows can reach embeddings when the floor misses them (lab values, doses, non-English). The ADR states this residual instead of 'never'.
- The claims rule rests on model judgment; the floor catches sensor-shaped values only.
- row_class holds value-free paraphrases, so forget must reach it by entry_id.
- Risk: medium, mostly classifier recall.

options.name: Full split: index and compaction take a value-free form
options.what: The previous recommendation. The transcript stays verbatim. The class gates every derived store: the index stores the value-free text for values rows and does not index pending rows; compaction input uses the value-free text; the nightly pass reads it; embeddings take none only. Compaction and B4 may flip only when the class switch is on and the backlog is empty.
options.pros:
- Smallest Art-9 footprint short of quarantine.
- Meets amendment:23 even if the index counts as long-term memory.
options.cons:
- Puts three M slices (index rewrite, entry-id re-derive, backlog) in front of compaction, which the owner already approved.
- Pending rows block the nightly mark, compaction spans and the global flip gate; a row the classifier keeps failing on stalls them.
- A late classify can write text derived from forgotten content back into the index unless fenced.
- Index text becomes a model paraphrase stored as an owner row, mislabelled in search and recall.
- Needs a post-delivery slot that does not exist yet.
- Size L. Risk: medium-high.

final.recommended: Light split: verbatim transcript and index, model class gates new stores and claims
final.reasoning:
Switch. Verifier 1's lighter option is better, and I confirmed its premises in source.

Why the light split:
- Every reader of the episode index puts text into model context: search_episodes, B3 recall (within recallReach), and the nightly model call (owner-do.ts:3031-3039). Ruling 2 allows that. The nightly pass's only persistent output is claims, so the guard belongs at the claim write.
- The index lives in the owner object beside the transcript, with the same forget, thread-erase and deleteAll reach (owner-do.ts:990-997, :2761-2778, :919). It adds no store and no lifetime the transcript does not already have.
- Compaction's input is the model view every turn already sends to the same provider with store:false (compaction.ts:82-85; llm/openai.ts:70). Its persisted output already meets policy (a) through the numeric floor (owner-turn.ts:741-746). So compaction needs only the owner's word, not a classifier.
- The new stores are where values would multiply: embeddings, which are invertible and deleted asynchronously, and claims, which ride every turn's system prompt (claims.ts:1056-1075, owner-turn.ts:546). The class is spent there.
- A failed or missing class fails closed (not embedded). Nothing waits on it. That removes the full split's stall, its global backlog gate and its post-delivery dependency.

The one reading this rests on: the owner treats the episode index as part of the transcript record, not as 'long-term memory' under amendment:23. If the owner reads it the other way, the full split (option 4) is the right choice. That is sub-decision A and falsifier 1.

Verifier findings, checked against source:
- Accepted: the every-turn prompt is turnMemoryPrompt, not the About-you block in memoryPrompt (claims.ts:1146, :1161, :1358 use memoryPrompt only for nightly, promotion and migration). The value in the prompt is observed in tests, so the [inference] tag is dropped.
- Accepted: the numeric floor misses lab values and doses, including the pinned fixture. Claims therefore rest on model instruction, with the floor as backstop. remember stays at internal_context. Switching to memory_block would redact contact facts and run the qualitative regexes, a fixed rule making a judgment call (sanitiser.ts:82-85, :585-590).
- Accepted: resolveSource is not wired (memory.ts:20, :101; owner-do.ts:2759-2780). S6 adds a resolver, checked against recallReach.
- Accepted: compactIfDue has no caller. The light split avoids needing a post-delivery slot: each owner turn's classify call also takes the previous reply row, and the nightly pass drains the rest.
- Accepted: iMessage history is not indexed (owner-do.ts:2820). In the light split the class writer wraps all three chain stores, independent of the index.
- Accepted: #1248 windows load(). Pending rows are found by SQL on row_class and fetched by entry id. S8 is sequenced after #1248.
- Accepted: a classify result must be fenced. settle() is a compare-and-set on row existence, source digest, pending state and consent epoch.
- Accepted: bounded retries. One retry owner (the nightly drain), an attempt count, and a terminal fail-closed state, unclassified.
- Accepted: 'never' in ADR-0081 means deterministic. The matrix row states 'model class plus numeric floor' and names the residual. The floor runs as a hard gate on every text entering embeddings.
- Accepted: retention and withdrawal amend ADR-0081 §3 and §5 for conversation rows. Withdrawal handling is mandatory before outside users, not optional. Model-use withdrawal is handled too (amendment:27).
- Accepted: scope widened to any person's health values and medication doses.
- Accepted: the class never widens a destination; class labels never go to logs, metrics, traces or audit.
- Accepted: the Brain steps. The matrix row travels inside the new ADR as an amendment of 0081, and the security-checklist exception goes through a canonical Brain edit and a remirror.
- Accepted: the falsifier sample. At least 150 values rows, reported as a confidence bound, with subsets.
- Accepted: the consent copy was over-promising; replaced.
- Accepted: account deletion already wipes the new table through deleteAll; no slice for it. ADR-0081 'never' sentence is line 80. Row 90 is cited as precedent.
- Moot under the switch: the index speaker label, the quoted/own split, the index backlog and mark stall, and the S5 resize. These applied only to the full split.
- Rejected: none outright. One partial correction: compaction still needs the B2 post-delivery call and the G43 eval before it flips. Those are B2's own dependencies, not G37's.

Sub-decisions the owner rules on with this:
- A: the episode index is part of the transcript record (recommended yes).
- B: claims hold a qualitative statement plus a pointer, decided by the model, with the floor as backstop (recommended yes, because a value in a claim rides every turn's prompt).
- C: before outside users, storage withdrawal rewrites values rows to their value-free form, and model-use withdrawal projects them value-free into model context (required by ADR-0081 §5 and amendment:27; the owner confirms).
- D: retention before outside users. Owner-typed values rows stay until deleted, following the row 90 precedent of quoted user intent. Waldo's reply rows that quote values are rewritten value-free after 90 days, matching the raw window (recommended).
- E: classify historical rows once, so B4 can embed old none rows. This re-sends past chat to the provider for a new purpose (recommended yes, owner-only beta).

Main trade-off: the index keeps verbatim values, for full search recall, in exchange for one owner reading. Everything new is gated by the model's class.
final.falsifier:
Any of these makes the light split the wrong choice.

1. Index reading. The owner, or a DPDP or App Store review, reads the episode index as long-term memory under HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:23. Then use the full split (option 4) for the index.

2. Classifier recall. Use synthetic sets of at least 150 values rows, 150 qualitative and 150 none. Subsets: third-party values, medication doses, Hindi, Marathi and mixed-language text, quoted content, Telegram-style and app-style. Run three times. Report the 95% upper bound, not only the point rate. The split fails for embeddings if the upper bound of values rows labelled none exceeds 3%, or any subset shows a values row labelled none in more than one run. Then B4 embeds no owner or quoted rows until a better classifier passes.

3. False positives. If more than 5% of none rows are labelled values, embedding recall suffers. Tune the instruction; this does not reopen the policy.

4. Claims. A scenario eval where the owner states lab values and doses. The split fails if remember or the nightly pass stores an exact value in more than 2 of 50 runs. Then the claim write needs a stronger guard, or exact values move to the health plane.

5. Legal. A review says owner-typed health values must not persist in Waldo's storage outside the RLS health plane. Then use option 1.

6. Cost. The classify call costs more than the turn's cheapest model call on a median turn. Then classify only in the nightly drain and record that 'classified at ingress' means 'pending at ingress'.

# ADR draft: health values in conversation rows (the transcript and its index keep them; a model class gates new stores and claims)

Status: Proposed. Decision packet G37. It is not authoritative until four things happen: the owner rules, it is published in Brain under the next free number (it carries the ADR-0081 matrix row in 2.8 as an amendment), the canonical security checklist in Brain is amended and remirrored, and `docs/foundation/accepted-adrs.json` is regenerated.

Source read at `beta-mvp` `e5c022ef`, Brain at `23c4f99`. File paths are under `packages/runtime/src/` unless named otherwise.

## 1. Context

**Where a value goes today.** A health value is a measurement, reading, score, lab result or medication dose. The owner may type one in chat, or Waldo may say one back in an owner-channel reply. Either way it is stored verbatim:

1. **The transcript row.** The canonical store scrubs only secret URLs (`conversation/canonical-owner-store.ts:19-22`, applied at `:150`). The Telegram store does the same (`channels/conversation-store.ts:54-56`). iMessage uses the canonical store (`channels/owner-do.ts:2820`).
2. **The episode index.** An FTS5 table in the owner object (`channels/episodes.ts:51`), fed by the Telegram and app stores (`owner-do.ts:2750`, `:2814`). Its readers all feed model context: `search_episodes`, B3 recall (`memory/turn-recall.ts:42-55`) and the nightly model call (`owner-do.ts:3031-3039`).
3. **Claims.** `remember` stores an owner-grounded claim and its quote (`tools/live/memory.ts:50-71`). Health is a profile kind (`memory/claims.ts:19-21`), so the claim enters every turn's system prompt through `turnMemoryPrompt` (`claims.ts:1056-1075`, called at `channels/owner-turn.ts:546`). Tests pin this (`test/memory-health-contact-route.test.ts:28`, `test/memory-health-owner-turn.test.ts:37-38`). The nightly instruction does not ask the model to leave numbers out (`claims.ts:1111`).

**What rejects health today.** The generic floor at `memory_block`, `r2_summary` and the other destinations (`packages/contracts/src/memory/sanitise.ts:349-362`). The numeric check on a compaction summary (`owner-turn.ts:745-746`), using `numericHealthIn` (`scribe/sanitiser.ts:90-91`). That predicate is English keyword regexes for sensor and score shapes. It misses lab values, doses and non-English text.

**The rules in force.**
- Ruling 2: the owner's readings and derived context may reach model context and owner-channel replies end to end (`docs/app/HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:7`).
- Long-term memory holds qualitative patterns plus a pointer (`:23`).
- Raw retention is 90 days; withdrawing model use stops health use in conversation (`:27`). Withdrawal-purge scope gates outside users (`:9`).
- CLAUDE.md line 11: whether a row is health is a judgment; no fixed rule decides it. Medication dosing is a hard boundary.
- CLAUDE.md line 23: sensitive chat is classified at ingress; never logs, audit, R2, browser jobs, third-party sends or drafts, tainted paths, or bulk long-term memory.
- ADR-0081: "never" means the schema and the sanitiser reject (line 80). A user-stated numeric goal persists in the DO as quoted user intent (row at line 90). Withdrawal deletes reconstructive residues, DO run residues included (lines 111, 113). Its matrix has no row for a value inside a conversation row.
- The retained contract asks for deterministic classification and a quarantine before any transcript write (`docs/planning/waldo-agent-mvp/IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACTS.md:16-17, :39`). It also requires generations that late writers check (`:37`, `:41`).

**Why this blocks features.** Semantic recall (B4) promises that health is never embedded, but no store knows which row is health. Compaction (B2) was waiting on whether its input may hold values.

**What the owner needs.** The app shows each row's text verbatim (`channels/app-api.ts:197-218`). The owner must see their own words on every device.

## 2. Decision

### 2.1 Scope
A conversation row carries a health value when it states a measurement, reading, score, lab result or medication dose about any person: the owner, family or anyone else. The model decides whether a row does.

### 2.2 The transcript and its index keep the row as written
- The transcript row stays verbatim in the store that holds the chain. The scrub stays secret-URL only.
- The episode index is part of the transcript record. It keeps rows verbatim, under the same forget, thread erase and account deletion as the transcript. Its readers feed model context only.
- The model window, recall and search read these rows under ruling 2, while model-use consent is active.
- Neither the row nor the index text goes to logs, audit records, R2, metrics, browser jobs, or third-party sends or drafts, unless the owner asks to share that item.

### 2.3 One class per row, from the model
- Each row gets one class: `none`, `qualitative` (health in words, no value) or `values`. For `values`, the answer also carries `value_free_text`: the row restated without any value, in the row's language.
- **When.** At ingress, beside the turn: one call per owner turn, never awaited by the reply. It classifies the new owner row and up to N pending rows of the chain, the previous reply included. CLAUDE.md line 23's "classified at ingress" is met by the pending record at persist and this call.
- **How.** Outside any SQLite transaction. `admit()` before the call and before the write. The purpose is metadata-only in the model-call log. The chat provider runs with `store: false`.
- **Retries.** The nightly pass is the one retry owner. It drains pending rows in bounded batches and counts attempts. After 3 failed attempts a row becomes `unclassified`, a terminal fail-closed state.
- No regex decides the class.

### 2.4 Where the class lives, and who writes it
- Table `row_class` in the owner object's SQLite: `entry_id` (primary key), `chain_ref`, `persisted_at`, `class` (pending, none, qualitative, values, unclassified), `value_free_text` (values rows only), `source_digest`, `consent_epoch`, `attempts`, `classified_at`.
- Its only writer is `conversation/row-class.ts`. A wrapper on all three chain stores writes `pending` when a row persists.
- **Fence.** A class answer commits only if, in the same commit, the source row still exists, its digest equals the digest sent to the model, the class is still `pending`, and the consent epoch is unchanged. Otherwise the answer is dropped.
- A row with no class row counts as not classified for every reader.
- **Never authority.** The class only narrows what a store receives. It never widens a destination and never authorises cross-surface replay, a send or a draft. Class labels never appear in logs, metrics, traces or audit; only content-free counts of pending and unclassified rows may.

### 2.5 What each store takes

| Store | `none` | `qualitative` | `values` | pending, unclassified or no class row |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Transcript and episode index | verbatim | verbatim | verbatim | verbatim |
| Compaction input | verbatim | verbatim | verbatim; the summary follows policy (a) and its numeric floor | verbatim |
| Embeddings (B4) | yes, if the text passes `numericHealthIn` | no | no | no |
| Claims | as today | qualitative claim | qualitative statement plus `source_ref`; never the value | qualitative statement plus `source_ref` |

- **Claims.** The `remember` description and the nightly instruction ask the model for a qualitative statement plus `source_ref`. `remember` keeps its `internal_context` destination. `numericHealthIn` runs explicitly in `remember` and in the nightly settle as the ADR-0024 Art-9 backstop. It catches sensor and score shapes only.
- **Exact value on demand.** `read_memory` may return the exact value from the source row, as model context, only when the chain's recall reach includes that row. Otherwise it returns the qualitative claim.
- **Existing claims.** A one-time model pass rewrites numeric health claims to the qualitative form and purges their `memory_backups` payloads.

### 2.6 Forget, deletion and withdrawal
- **Forget.** A forget hit on a row's text redacts it literally in the transcript, the index and `value_free_text`. The row's class is then reset to `pending` and re-derived from the redacted row, because a paraphrase can carry a topic without its words.
- **Embeddings.** A forget settles only after the vector delete is read back.
- **Deletion.** Thread erase removes class rows. Account deletion wipes them through `storage.deleteAll()`.
- **Storage withdrawal (required before any outside user).** A consent signal reaches the owner object and advances the consent generation before any purge. Each `values` row in the transcript and index is rewritten to its `value_free_text`, with its witness, in one unit. `unclassified` and unclassed rows get the fixed marker `[health details removed]`.
- **Model-use withdrawal (required before any outside user).** Values rows are projected value-free into the model window, recall and search at read time. The exact-value read is off.

### 2.7 Retention (amends ADR-0081 §3 for conversation rows)
- Owner-typed rows that carry values stay until the owner deletes the message, thread or account, or forgets it. Precedent: ADR-0081's user-stated goal row, kept as quoted user intent.
- Waldo's reply rows that carry values are rewritten to their `value_free_text` after 90 days, matching the raw window. This runs before any outside user; during owner-only beta it does not.

### 2.8 ADR-0081 matrix row (amendment carried by this ADR)

| Field class | Canonical destination and retention | Authenticated product surface | Prompt / DO / R2 / memory / trace eligibility | External-channel eligibility |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Health value inside a conversation row (owner-typed, or in Waldo's owner-channel reply; about any person) | The owner's transcript row and its episode index in the owner object. Owner-typed rows: until deleted or forgotten. Reply rows: value-free after 90 days. Withdrawal per 2.6. | The owner's own transcript | Model context: yes while model-use consent is active (ruling 2). Embeddings: excluded by model class plus the numeric floor; residual: misclassified values the floor does not match, in any language. Compaction summary: qualitative only, numeric floor. Claims: qualitative plus pointer, model-judged, numeric floor backstop. R2, logs, audit, metrics: never (schema and sanitiser). Traces: the staging exception only. | Only when the owner asks to share that item |

### 2.9 The switch
`ROW_CLASS.enabled` gates classification. Off, no class rows are written, and B4 embeds no rows (no class means no embedding). Compaction does not depend on it.

## 3. Considered Options

1. **Quarantine at ingress** (the retained contract, with model classification in place of DLP). The strongest Art-9 posture. Rejected for now: a crash window before persist, a hosted migration, an app.v1 change, markers on the owner's own screen, and [inference] the value has already crossed the channel and the provider. It returns if a legal or App Store review forbids owner-typed values in Waldo's own storage.
2. **Verbatim everywhere.** Rejected: it breaks `HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:23` and compaction policy (a), puts health text into an invertible embedding store (Morris et al., EMNLP 2023: 92% exact recovery of 32-token inputs on the models tested), and Vectorize deletes are asynchronous.
3. **This decision.** The transcript and index stay verbatim; the class gates embeddings and claims.
4. **Full split.** The index, compaction input and nightly pass take a value-free form. Rejected for now: it puts three slices in front of compaction, pending rows stall search, nightly and compaction, and index paraphrases read as the owner's words. It becomes the choice if the owner reads the index as long-term memory.

## 4. Consequences

- **Benefits.**
  - The owner sees their words verbatim on every surface.
  - Compaction is unblocked by this ruling alone.
  - "Health never embedded" and "qualitative plus pointer" become enforceable, decided by the model, with a stated residual.
  - Exact values leave the every-turn system prompt.
  - No app.v1, Supabase, wrangler or edge change.
  - A3 visibility can read the class later, to narrow only.
- **Costs and risks.**
  - One cheap model call per owner turn. [inference] Small; the build PR reports tokens per turn.
  - The index keeps values as long as the transcript does.
  - Misclassified values the floor misses can reach embeddings.
  - The claims rule rests mostly on model judgment.
  - `row_class` holds value-free paraphrases, so forget must reach it.
  - Two pinned memory tests change.
- **Amended text.**
  - ADR-0081 §3 (matrix and retention) and §5 (withdrawal), for conversation rows, through 2.6-2.8.
  - `IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACTS.md:16`, `:17` and `:39` are superseded for rows in the owner's own channel. `:37` and `:41` stand; the fence in 2.4 and the generation in 2.6 meet them.
  - The security checklist's "no health values in DO SQLite tables" gets an exception for the owner's transcript and index, through a canonical Brain edit and remirror.
- **Impact surface.** New `conversation/row-class.ts`; `channels/owner-turn.ts`; `channels/owner-do.ts` (store wiring, erase, classifier host, nightly drain, hideHistory, resolver, consent signal); `memory/claims.ts`; `tools/live/memory.ts`; `channels/app-health.ts`; `conversation/canonical-owner-store.ts`; `channels/conversation-store.ts`; `channels/episodes.ts`; the B4 vector outbox; tests for each.

## 5. Verification and tests

All fixtures are synthetic. None carries a real value.

- **Class.** Each persisted row on all three chain stores gets exactly one `row_class` row. A `values` row's `value_free_text` contains no reading.
- **Fence.** Forget, thread erase and withdrawal each land between the classify call and its commit. No class row and no `value_free_text` survive.
- **Terminal state.** A classifier that always fails leaves the row `unclassified` after 3 attempts. Nothing else waits on it. Only content-free counts are logged.
- **Ingress.** The classify call does not delay the reply (trace assertion on hop order). A closed run writes nothing.
- **I/O order.** The model call runs outside the SQLite transaction.
- **Embeddings.** Conformance: a `qualitative`, `values`, pending, `unclassified` or unclassed row never reaches the embedding call. A `none` row whose text trips `numericHealthIn` is not embedded. Vector deletes are read back before a forget settles.
- **Claims.**
  - A sensor-shaped value in `remember` text or evidence is refused with the qualitative-plus-pointer instruction.
  - Scenario eval: the owner states a lab value and a dose; the stored claim is qualitative with a `source_ref`.
  - `read_memory` returns the exact value from the source row in reach, and the qualitative claim when the row is in a private thread out of reach.
  - The one-time pass leaves no numeric health claim and no matching `memory_backups` payload.
  - The two pinned tests are rewritten red first.
- **Forget.** A topic present only in a `values` row is forgotten from the transcript, the index and `value_free_text`, and resurfaces nowhere after re-derive.
- **Withdrawal.** Storage withdrawal leaves no `values` row verbatim in any chain store or the index. Model-use withdrawal sends value-free text to the model and disables the exact-value read.
- **Retention.** A Waldo reply row with values older than 90 days is rewritten value-free; an owner-typed row is not.
- **App.** The transcript page returns the owner's row verbatim, with no app.v1 change.
- **Hostile.** A row that tells the classifier to mark it `none` is classed by its content. A malformed answer counts as a failed attempt.
- **Concurrent.** Two turns on one chain settle classes without loss or duplication.
- **Classifier eval (the falsifier).** At least 150 rows per class, with subsets for third-party values, doses, Hindi, Marathi and mixed text, and quoted content. Three runs. Report the 95% upper bound. Flip bar: upper bound of values rows labelled `none` at most 3%, and no subset with a values row labelled `none` in more than one run; `none` rows labelled `values` at most 5%.

## 6. Rollback

- `ROW_CLASS.enabled = false` stops new class writes. B4 then embeds no rows, because no class means no embedding. Compaction is unaffected.
- Existing class rows stay and are ignored. They hold no values.
- Claims already in pointer form stay valid.
- No hosted data changes, so no data rollback is needed. Rolling back reopens G37 for B4.

verdicts.betterOption: A lighter version of the split, contingent on one owner reading. The owner rules that the transcript and its FTS episode index both keep rows verbatim. The index lives in the same owner object, under the same forget, thread-erase and deleteAll reach, so it adds no store and no lifetime. Compaction then flips on its already-approved policy (a), with no new gate. The content-free per-row class from S3 is still written at ingress, but only B4's 'embed none only' rule and A3 visibility read it. Claims get 'qualitative plus pointer' from model instruction, with the numeric floor as backstop. Every reader of the episode index except the nightly pass is model context, which ruling 2 allows, and the nightly pass's output is guarded at the claim write. So this drops S2's index rewrite, S4's entry-id re-derive and S5's backlog: roughly three M-sized slices plus the switch-on recall regression. It also unblocks the owner's top pain, 'loses context', now rather than after S2-S6. The packet's split stays the better choice only if the owner reads the episode index as 'long-term memory' under HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:23.

blocking: Classification has no source or deletion generation fence. A classify call in flight during a forget, thread erase or withdrawal can commit after it and write index_text (and a class) derived from the deleted or pre-redaction text. That puts forgotten or erased content back into the searchable index.

A pending row has no terminal state and no attempt bound, and three different paths retry it. One row the classifier keeps failing on (a malformed answer, a refusal, a provider outage, or adversarial input) stays pending forever. The consequences: it is re-sent to the model every turn; it holds the nightly mark, so memory consolidation stops for the whole owner; it blocks every compaction span that contains it, with no attempt counted; and it keeps the global 'backlog empty' gate shut for compaction and B4. This breaks bounded work, the one-retry-owner rule and honest terminal ambiguity.

The proposed ADR-0081 matrix row says derived stores 'never' get the value. In ADR-0081, 'never' means the schema and the sanitiser reject the field. Here only the model's class enforces it. A values row misclassed as none or qualitative goes verbatim into the index, the compaction input and the nightly pass. A none row goes into embeddings with no deterministic check at all. The numeric backstop runs only on a values row's index_text, and its patterns are English-only. The owners write in English, Hindi and Marathi.

The ADR quietly amends ADR-0081's retention and withdrawal rules for health values inside transcript rows, and never says so. This covers Waldo's own replies that quote wearable readings. Those copies would live in DO storage indefinitely, while the same reading in the health plane is deleted after its retention window. Accepted ADR-0081 §5 requires withdrawal to delete reconstructive residues. Yet sub-decision C is offered with 'C no: withdrawal leaves chat rows untouched' as an acceptable answer.

final.adrMarkdown:
# ADR draft: the nightly model-graded eval (hosting, judge, spend, scorecards)

Status: Proposed, 14 Oct 2026. It becomes authoritative only after three things:
1. the owner approves it;
2. it is published in Brain under the next free number (0085 at the Brain checkout read, unless another draft takes it);
3. `docs/foundation/accepted-adrs.json` is regenerated.

It applies ADR-0069's harness rules to a second, nightly harness. It extends ADR-0069 in two named places (sections 2.2 and 2.3). It changes no roster pin, product route or runtime path.

Author: the decision-packet session. Source read at `beta-mvp` `04bb8c89`. PR #1185 merged as `90ed0786`; nothing under `packages/runtime/evals` or `.github/workflows` changed between the two.

## 1. Context

- **Before #1185.** The only model-graded eval was `packages/runtime/evals/run.ts`. It runs by hand, runs one trial, and is graded by the model it tests (`run.ts:31`). A change that keeps the tool trajectory but makes replies worse goes unseen (harness comparison, section 9.2).
- **#1185 (merged)** adds `packages/runtime/evals/nightly/`:
  - 22 synthetic scenarios: 19 runnable, 3 reported blocked;
  - three trials each, reported as pass^3;
  - an Anthropic Messages API judge with a fixed thinking budget;
  - one call budget shared by the candidate and the judge.

  It has no workflow, key, schedule, storage, dollar figure or release tie. Those are owner decisions, recorded here.
- **ADR-0069 sets most of the rules:**
  - the harness judge is cross-family `claude-haiku-4-5`, scoped to comparative judging;
  - no judge is trusted until TPR and TNR are both at least 0.85 against the founder's blind labels, with honeypots so the fail class has at least 25 cases, and with binomial CIs;
  - any judge or rubric change, or any deprecation notice on a pinned ID, re-runs the labels;
  - synthetic-only harness traffic needs no Anthropic DPA;
  - harness runs are off-peak;
  - the product Anthropic key lives in gateway BYOK, never in Worker env.
- **Facts that shape the design:**
  - The repository is public.
  - GitHub fires a scheduled workflow only from the default branch, `main`, which has diverged from `beta-mvp` by thousands of commits. Neither branch is protected.
  - The judge's fixed thinking budget is rejected with a 400 by current-generation Anthropic models; Haiku 4.5 accepts it.
  - Tokens are summed per role today, so cost cannot be computed.
  - A scenario counts as graded if any one trial was graded, so a mostly ungraded night still prints a pass rate.
- **Waiting on this:** the compaction switch (its draft, section 6), the semantic-recall switch, persona rubrics and release suites.

## 2. Decision

### 2.1 Hosting
- **The workflow.** `nightly-eval.yml` runs on `schedule` and on `workflow_dispatch` with an optional `source_sha` input.
  - The same file lives on `main` (for the schedule) and on `beta-mvp`.
  - It always checks out `beta-mvp`, or `source_sha` when given; never the dispatched ref.
  - `source_sha` goes through env, must match 40 lowercase hex characters, and must be an ancestor of `origin/beta-mvp`.
- **Hardening.**
  - `permissions: contents: read`;
  - every action pinned to a full SHA;
  - no `pull_request_target`;
  - one `concurrency` group, so runs never overlap;
  - `timeout-minutes: 120`.
- **Keys.**
  - The two CI keys live only as environment secrets of the GitHub environment `nightly-eval`, limited to `main` and `beta-mvp`.
  - They are mapped into the eval step's env only, never job env, so install lifecycle scripts never see them.
  - They never go into Worker env, wrangler or repository-level secrets.
- **Schedule:** `17 21 * * *` (21:17 UTC, 02:47 IST). That is off-peak for the owner's zone [inference: IST], off the top of the hour, and done before morning.
- **No transcripts in CI.** `WALDO_EVAL_ONLY` and `WALDO_EVAL_EXPORT_DIR` are never set there.
- **Branch protection.** Either a ruleset requires a reviewed pull request on `beta-mvp` and `main`, or the owner's written acceptance of unreviewed push access is recorded here: `<owner ruling>`.

### 2.2 Judge
- **The model.** The judge is `claude-haiku-4-5`, called directly on the Anthropic Messages API with thinking on.
  - The code defaults to `ROSTER.harness_judge`.
  - An override must be an Anthropic roster model that accepts `budget_tokens`.
- **Extension of ADR-0069.** This ADR widens the `harness_judge` role from comparative judging to absolute pass/fail grading on the nightly rubric.
  - ADR-0069's comparative calibration does not carry over.
  - The nightly rubric gets its own founder-label calibration.
  - The rubric version is pinned by `catalogue_digest`. Any digest change re-runs the labels before any switch may flip on a scorecard.
- **Preflight.** One judge call on a fixed synthetic packet runs before any candidate call. A 4xx aborts the night with zero candidate spend.
- **Honeypots.** About 15 synthetic records that must fail are judged every night. A honeypot graded pass, or returning a judge error, counts as not caught.
- **Calibration.**
  - The owner labels a locally run, blind export (transcripts and verdicts in separate files).
  - The set has at least 25 fail cases (organic plus honeypots).
  - TPR and TNR are reported with 95% CIs. The judge is trusted at 0.85 or above on both, with every honeypot caught.
  - Calibration week also runs three dispatches at one pinned `source_sha` to measure noise.
- **Migration target.** `claude-haiku-5-5` with adaptive thinking is the named target when Haiku 4.5 gets a deprecation notice or fails calibration. It needs a code change, a roster amendment and its own calibration.

### 2.3 Keys and spend
- **A second Anthropic key home.** ADR-0069 keeps the product Anthropic key in gateway BYOK. This ADR adds eval-only Anthropic keys in GitHub (CI) and with the backend lead (local calibration). They are scoped to a `waldo-evals` workspace. This keeps eval spend out of the product gateway's route budgets and keeps the product gateway token out of CI.
- **Three limits; the tightest wins.**
  1. **Per run.** `WALDO_EVAL_MAX_CALLS` is 600 for the first run. After that it is 1.25 x the measured calls, rounded up to tens.
  2. **Per month, at the provider.** Anthropic: a `waldo-evals` workspace spend limit of $100, with a notification at $50. OpenAI: the control actually verified in force, recorded here as `<owner ruling: project hard limit, or a prepaid-credit eval-only organization>`, at $50. Until it is verified, the per-run cap is the binding OpenAI limit.
  3. **Time.** The job timeout.
- **Visible cost.** The scorecard reports estimated dollars per role from separate input, output and cached token counts.
- **Rotation.** All eval keys are revoked and reissued on removal of any collaborator with write access, on suspected workflow tampering, and every 90 days.

### 2.4 Scorecards and the release tie
- **Fields.** Each card carries:
  - `source_sha`: the checked-out commit, never `github.sha`;
  - `catalogue_digest`;
  - the candidate and judge model ids;
  - `started_at` and `finished_at`;
  - counts and rates;
  - ungraded and judge-error totals by class (status family or parse; never body text);
  - tokens split into input, output and cached;
  - estimated dollars;
  - honeypots caught.

  It never carries text.
- **Storage.** Each run uploads the artifact `nightly-eval-<source_sha>-<run_id>`, kept 90 days, and writes a job-summary table.
- **Release tie.**
  - The deploy hand-off dispatches `nightly-eval` with `source_sha` set to the reviewed release SHA.
  - The lead commits that card under `docs/evals/nightly/<sha>.json`, kept indefinitely; it holds counts only.
  - If no card's `source_sha` equals the deployed `WALDO_RELEASE`, the hand-off states 'no scorecard for this release'.
- **Exit status.** The run exits non-zero when:
  - ungraded trials exceed 10% of runnable trials;
  - nothing was graded;
  - the budget ran out;
  - the preflight failed; or
  - a honeypot was not caught.

  A low pass rate is not a failure. The trajectory tests stay the merge gate.

### 2.5 Data
- **Synthetic only, enforced.** Every scenario, honeypot and compaction script is authored synthetic. A case derived from a real conversation is rewritten and reviewed, never pasted.
  - A guard test fails if any fixture address or domain is not `.example` or `example.com`, or if a phone-number pattern appears.
  - This is the deterministic boundary that the no-DPA exemption rests on.
- **Providers.** Anthropic receives synthetic transcripts, tool names, effects and final state. OpenAI receives synthetic turns with `store: false`. Both fall under ADR-0069's synthetic-only exemption. This grants no DPA standing to any other traffic.
- **Public by default.** Logs, summaries and artifacts are public in this repository. The card holds no text. The owner accepts that pass rates are public.

## 3. Considered options

1. **GitHub Actions, direct Haiku 4.5 judge, eval-only keys, provider spend controls** (above). Chosen: no roster pin change, the merged code works as written, and spend and keys stay out of product paths.
2. **A current-generation judge with adaptive thinking.**
   - Haiku 5.5 costs about a tenth of Haiku 4.5's judge cost [inference]. Sonnet 5.5 or Opus 5.5 is probably stronger [inference] and costs more.
   - All of them reject the fixed thinking budget, so this needs a code change, a roster amendment and its own calibration.
   - Kept as the migration and fallback path.
3. **Judge through the existing AI Gateway with the product BYOK key.**
   - Pro: one key home, with payload logging off.
   - Cons: eval spend would draw on product route budgets that the Haiku fallback relies on; CI would hold the product gateway token; the chat-completions path may not pass Anthropic thinking [inference].

4. **A second OpenAI model as judge.** Same-family judging is what ADR-0069 avoids, and the roster has no second OpenAI model. Rejected.

It needs provider keys in Worker env, which ADR-0069 forbids, plus wrangler and deploy changes and synthetic owners in staging storage. Rejected for the nightly run. Revisit for release suites against a deployed build.
6. **Manual runs only.** Regressions surface only when someone remembers. Used for the first run and for calibration.

## 4. Consequences

- **Benefits:**
  - a nightly, cross-family pass^3 measurement tied to exact source, including every released SHA;
  - the compaction and recall switches get a real-model bar;
  - cost is visible on every card and capped at more than one layer.
- **Costs:**
  - about $60-95 a month [inference];
  - one vendor workspace and four eval keys (two in a public repository's environment, two with the lead);
  - about 2 hours of owner labelling once, and again after any catalogue, judge or deprecation change.
- **Risks:**
  - Without the ruleset, anyone with write access can run code with the eval keys. The eval-only spend controls bound the damage.
  - GitHub can delay, drop or auto-disable scheduled runs. A missed night shows as a missing artifact.
  - A card describes source run in process, not the running deploy.
  - Haiku 4.5 is previous-generation, so a second calibration is likely when it is deprecated.
- **Impact surface:**
  - `packages/runtime/evals/nightly/*` and its tests;
  - `.github/workflows/nightly-eval.yml` on two branches;
  - the deploy hand-off comment and runbook;
  - `docs/evals/nightly/`.

  No runtime, contract, migration, wrangler or app change.

## 5. Decisions the owner makes

1. Anthropic as the eval judge vendor, under the synthetic-only exemption.
2. The second, direct Anthropic key home for evals.
3. Widening `harness_judge` to absolute nightly grading.
4. Hosting on GitHub Actions in this public repository, with public, text-free scorecards.
5. Branch protection, or written acceptance of the risk.
6. The caps, and which OpenAI control is in force.
7. The schedule.
8. Retention.
9. The calibration labels.

## 6. Verification and tests

- **Config:**
  - a judge override outside the allowed Anthropic roster set throws;
  - live mode without `WALDO_EVAL_SOURCE_SHA` throws.
- **Preflight:** a stubbed 400 aborts with zero candidate calls and a non-zero exit.
- **Honeypots:**
  - a stub judge that passes everything fails the run;
  - a honeypot returning judge_error counts as not caught;
  - a correct judge catches all of them.
- **Card:**
  - all new fields are present;
  - no scenario text, mail field or address appears;
  - a rubric edit changes the digest;
  - dollars match modelCost on a fixed token split.
- **Exit status:**
  - 50 judge errors in 57 trials exits non-zero;
  - a budget-exhausted night exits non-zero;
  - a graded night with failures exits zero.
- **Synthetic guard:** a fixture with a non-`.example` address fails the test.
- **Workflow review:**
  - every `uses:` is pinned to a full SHA;
  - `permissions` is `contents: read`;
  - the secrets appear only in the eval step's env;
  - `source_sha` is never interpolated into `run:`;
  - a non-hex or non-ancestor `source_sha` fails before install;
  - a dispatch from `main` still checks out `beta-mvp`.
- **First live run:** about 19 graded and 3 blocked, every honeypot caught, and the card's dollars within about 20% of both provider usage pages.
- **Calibration:**
  - at least 25 fail labels;
  - TPR and TNR at 0.85 or above with CIs reported;
  - no more than 3 of 19 pass^3 flips across three runs at one pinned SHA.
- **Falsifiers that reopen this decision:**
  - calibration below the bar (move to option 2);
  - the noise check above;
  - more than $150 a month across both accounts;
  - more than 2 of 7 nights with no artifact;
  - a ruling that synthetic traffic still needs a DPA (the eval stays manual until signed).

## 7. Rollback

1. Disable the workflow: Actions > nightly-eval > Disable workflow. Or delete the file on both branches.
2. Revoke all four eval keys at the providers.
3. Delete the `nightly-eval` environment.

Nothing in the runtime depends on the eval. Committed release cards stay as history.

options.what: Keep every consequential effect behind a desk card. Close G3 as 'not this release'.
options.pros: No new authority surface or code. The card is already stronger than LangGraph's re-run and on par with the Agent SDK defer (harness §6.1). Nothing to get wrong.
options.cons: Waldo still never acts without asking. The Window (ADR-0019) and Patrol stay proposal-only, and approval fatigue grows with Patrol and C7 errands. The 'already on it' focus-protection job never ships. Risk: low for safety, high for product.

options.name: B. Narrow closed-class grants on the owner object, desk-owned, gated by run origin; first class calendar.move_own_block
options.what: A standing_grants table on the owner object with a single writer. A grant is created only by approving a new desk card kind, standing_grant. A closed class enum ships one class: move a block Waldo created (proven by an exact ledger create record), with no attendees, on the owner's primary calendar, inside an owner-set window, weekdays, minimum lead and daily cap, with a required expiry. Eligibility depends on an immutable run-origin field (an owner-authored turn or an owner timer job; never an externally woken run or a reply to someone else), not on the accumulated turn taint. The host re-checks the grant inside the effect ledger's reserve transaction through a new authorize callback. Uses are counted by the existing quota seam, keyed by class and connection. Authority never crosses a wake. Revocation is immediate. Every use gets a host-built receipt and an etag-guarded undo. Off by default, and hard-off in production in code.
options.pros: Meets every CLAUDE.md grant clause using seams that exist: the desk, the ledger quota, the derived create id, etag moves and responsibilities.grant_ref. Sends nothing to anyone, and the effect is reversible (ADR-0019). Reuses PR #932's best invariants and tests. Needs no hosted migration, wrangler change or secret. Each later class is an ADR amendment. Doubles as ADR-0074's graduation-gate evidence for one effect.

Calendar or other external text read in an eligible run can steer a move inside the bounds. That is the accepted risk, mitigated by cap, window, lead, receipts and undo, not by taint. A move changes free/busy that colleagues can see. The work touches approvals.ts and google.ts, which are Connectors-lane hot files under the A0 ratchet, and needs an app contract pin before emitting. final.reasoning:
Hypotheses considered:
- (1) A broad grant model pays off fastest (C).
- (2) A global slider is enough (D).
- (3) A narrow first class on the existing desk and ledger seams gives real autonomy with a bounded blast radius (B).
- (4) Grants are not needed yet (A).

Evidence against C and D:
- Both cover sends to other people, which are irreversible. Email "can't be undone" (approvals.ts:598). Moving events with guests emails them.
- The release brief forbids sends, spending, deletes, sharing and health destinations.
- CLAUDE.md:20 requires per-resource, parameter, time and budget scope. A slider has none.

Evidence against A: the Window job (ADR-0019) and Patrol only matter if Waldo can act unattended somewhere. A gives no path there.

Why B:
1. The seams exist. The desk freezes and digests payloads and already reads the event before a move. The ledger already reserves intent and quota in one synchronous transaction (owner-effect-ledger.ts:43-70), so the grant recheck is a sync SQL read inside it, with no external I/O.
2. "Waldo's own block" is provable from the ledger, using an exact create record and the derived id (approvals.ts:771), not a marker other apps could write.
3. The effect sends nothing and can be undone: no attendees, times only, etag-guarded undo. The move schema already refuses description, location and attendees (calendar.ts:23-25).
4. One writer per aggregate holds. The grant module writes grants, the desk writes rows, and the ledger writes intents and counts uses. v0.5 authority_grants stays untouched; it runs only in local run-loop environments anyway (run-loop/do.ts:376-378).
5. It gives ADR-0074 what it asks for before any L3 activation: a contract update (this ADR) and conformance proof (S5).

Verifier findings: accepted.
- Taint (blocking, verifier 1). Confirmed at conversation/tool-loop.ts:208-215: an external-stamped result taints the rest of the turn. query_calendar is external-origin. So the old check 3 ("argument taint is null") would card almost every move, and the claim that "a timer pass is untainted" was wrong. Fix: eligibility now depends on an immutable run-origin field set at turn start, separate from the accumulated toolArgSourceTaint. The ADR now says plainly, in §2.3 and §2.8, that external text read in an eligible run can steer moves inside the bounds, and that ADR-0049's taint is not the control for this class.
- I rejected the "null-taint own-block read" alternative. To decide where a block should move, the model must still read other events (the conflicting meeting), and those are third-party text. Removing taint from one read would hide the steering risk, not remove it.
- ADR-0074 graduation gate. Accepted and named.
- Connectors lane co-ownership. Accepted.
- Tool description and status text. Accepted.
- Stale results consume the cap. Confirmed: they are recorded as done. I chose to count them, which fails closed and needs no ledger change. This is documented and tested.
- Missing desk columns, the undo sites and the LIMIT 5. Confirmed and added to S3.
- Coordinator built only in local environments. Confirmed; this strengthens the case against option 4.
- PR #932 test count corrected.
- No code creates Window blocks. Confirmed; a pre-count step added.
- Production hard-off (blocking, verifier 2). Accepted. Modeled on trace-privacy.ts:62-66.
- authorize applies only to a reserved-to-attempting transition. Accepted. Reconciliation of attempting or unknown records is never blocked.
- Host-built summaries so the model's reason never reaches activity, hops or the grant row. Accepted.
- Free/busy visibility is shown on the card and named as an ADR-0018 amendment. Accepted.
- Exact ownership proof. Accepted. Card-approved moves also write calendar_change records (approvals.ts:775-777).
- Quota keyed by class and connection, so a superseding grant cannot reset the day. Accepted.
- Console revoke behind the console session. Accepted.
- Disclosure copy owner step. Accepted.

Verifier findings: rejected in part.
- Verifier 2 said taint is a per-run stamp that in-run reads never raise. That is wrong (tool-loop.ts:208-215). Its conclusion still holds under the new origin rule: unattended timer runs can be steered. That is now owner decision §5.6.
- Verifier 2 said deletion does not reach the grant store. That is wrong. Owner deletion runs storage.deleteAll() on the owner object (owner-do.ts:919, 1483, 1611), which removes the new table. A regression test is added. No owner data export exists to extend [inference from grep]. The ADR says any future export must include grants.

Main trade-off: B gives the least immediate relief, and it openly accepts bounded steering by external text in place of a card. That is deliberate. The first standing permission should be one whose worst case is a capped, undoable change to the owner's own focus time.

Threshold to proceed: the owner accepts the never-list, the defaults and the §5.6 run-origin choice. S3 tests must show authorize runs inside reserve with no awaited I/O. Confidence: about 70%. The main uncertainty is reach: today no code creates Window blocks, so the class is only worth building alongside a Window-block create path, or if owner-approved attendee-free creates are common.
final.falsifier:
Any one of these makes B the wrong choice.

1. In 20 runs each of the hostile scenarios (an invite whose description tells Waldo to move focus blocks, read in an owner turn, a standing-order fire and a timer pass), any grant-run move lands outside the owner window, inside the minimum lead, or above the daily cap. The bounds are then not enforced at the host.
2. The grant recheck cannot run inside the ledger reserve transactionSync without awaited I/O. Recheck-at-dispatch then fails CLAUDE.md:18, and A should stand until it can.
3. The pre-count of existing attendee-free, non-recurring create records on beta owner objects is near zero, and no Window-block create path is planned. 4. The app cannot pin the additive contract (the standing_grant kind and the grants routes) before the backend needs to emit. The first release must then stay switch-off.
5. A multi-use grant already exists under another name (harness doc §13). This ADR then becomes a review of that path.
